facts.text: For camera hardware-in-the-loop testing, RAW-data injection advocates cite monitor synchronization and field-of-view problems, whereas projector-stimulation advocates claim the gap is closing. Both positions are vendor views based on on-road evidence.
facts.quote: Injection advocates cite monitor sync and field-of-view problems; projector advocates claim the gap is closing. Both positions are vendor views.

facts.text: For radar minimum simulated range, a 2021 peer-reviewed review reports about 20 to 30 m for digital target simulators, whereas vendors claim 0.6 m. The disagreement is partly attributable to digital versus analog or hybrid architectures; the review notes that analog simulators reach very low minimum ranges.
facts.quote: The 2021 peer-reviewed review gives about 20 to 30 m for digital target simulators; vendors claim 0.6 m.

facts.text: DetZero and CTRL claim that auto-labels surpass average human labels, whereas other authors stress dependence on human-labeled training data and the risk of silent systematic error. These positions are presented as independent on-road evidence.
facts.quote: DetZero and CTRL claim to surpass average human labels, while other authors stress dependence on human-labeled training data and the risk of silent systematic error.

facts.text: Physical or raw sensor simulation catches perception errors but is expensive, whereas semantic object injection enables huge coverage but assumes perception succeeded. Neither test approach dominates.
facts.quote: Physical or raw sensor simulation catches perception errors but is expensive; semantic object injection enables huge coverage but assumes perception succeeded. Neither dominates.

facts.text: To resolve the trade-off between raw-sensor realism and scalable semantic simulation, the defensible approach is to allocate each safety requirement to the lowest-cost test level containing its failure mechanisms, then correlate those models using higher-fidelity levels.
facts.quote: The defensible approach is to allocate each safety requirement to the lowest-cost test level that contains its failure mechanisms, then use higher-fidelity levels to correlate those models.

facts.text: On how conservative intervention should be, regulators require fail-to-safe, whereas the University of Pretoria and industry report production losses and resistance caused by false interventions.
facts.quote: Regulators require fail-to-safe; the University of Pretoria and the industry report production losses and resistance due to false interventions.

facts.text: On field time needed after extensive simulation, statistical planning supports claim-driven sample sizes rather than mileage folklore. No fixed field-time number applies independently of required detection rate, tolerated false-alarm rate, scenario distribution and confidence target.
facts.quote: No fixed number applies independently of the required detection rate, tolerated false-alarm rate, scenario distribution and confidence target; statistical planning supports claim-driven sample sizes rather than mileage folklore.

facts.text: Simulation and common software encourage grouping machine variants into equivalence classes, whereas differences in sensor mounting, machine envelope, payload, brake dynamics, articulation and occlusion can defeat those equivalence claims.
facts.quote: Simulation and common software encourage equivalence classes; sensor mounting, machine envelope, payload, brake dynamics, articulation and occlusion can defeat them.

facts.text: In the disagreement over grouping machine variants into families, a family claim should identify invariant parameters and parameters bounded by worst-case physical confirmation.
facts.quote: A family claim should state which parameters are invariant and which are bounded by worst-case physical confirmation.

facts.text: HUGSIM and pseudo-simulation proponents favor neural re-simulation, whereas XLD benchmark authors find large gaps for off-trajectory views. The disagreement is supported by independent on-road evidence.
facts.quote: Proponents (HUGSIM, pseudo-simulation) versus benchmark authors (XLD) who find large gaps for off-trajectory views.
